newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot natgas prices fall ahead of weekend.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot natgas prices fall ahead of weekend.

text.p: U.S. spot natural gas prices were five to 10 cents lower Friday after more than a week of rallying as traders anticipated a drop in demand for the weekend and early next week, sources said.
Gulf Coast gas prices softened by about five cents into the $2.31-2.36 per million British thermal units range, with the higher-priced deals done mostly in early trading.
Temperatures are expected to moderate in the eastern and midwestern U.S. beginning Sunday, with a return of below-normal temperatures to the Northeast forecast to surface later next week.

In the Midcontinent, prices softened by about 10 cents today into the $2.08-2.13 area as forecasters called for temperatures to be four to eight degrees Fahrenheit above-normal in the region from Saturday through Monday.
At the Chicago city-gate, prices fell into the mid-to-high $2.50s, also down about 10 cents from Thursday.

In west Texas, prices dipped to about the $2.10 area, down about 10 cents on the day. Sources attributed the weakness to cooler West Coast weather, more Canadian gas available and the return of the 350 megawatt unit 2 at the San Juan coal-fired power plant in New Mexico.
Also loosening the market was the expected restart on Saturday of Southern California Edison's 1,080 MW unit 2 at the San Onofre nuclear plant.

These factors pressured prices at the southern California border more severely, as traders closing deals early in the $2.15-20 range but in the $2.08-2.13 area late, plummeting about 15 cents from Thursday.

Despite the drop in cash, prices on the Gulf Coast are still up about 25 cents from last Friday, fueled by some early heating demand and production cuts due to Tropical Storm Josephine earlier in the week.
